problems.title: Hou-Zeng conjecture (PPL 013)
problems.statement: Every integer n > 4 can be written as n = p + F + C, p an odd prime, F a positive Fibonacci number, C a Catalan number.
problems.source: Z.-W. Sun, arXiv:0901.3075, Conjecture 1.13; OEIS A154404. Prize: $1000 proof / $200 counterexample (verify original terms).

prize.reward: $1,000 for a proof / $200 for a verified counterexample (per Sun's list)
prize.status: Open. Checked to ~3e13 in the literature; a counterexample is extremely unlikely. Original prize terms not yet verified.

problems.title: Erdős minimum overlap problem (upper bound)
problems.statement: Find a step function h on [0,2] with values in [0,1] and integral 1 minimising max_k ∫h(x)(1−h(x+k))dx. Its value is an upper bound on the Erdős minimum overlap constant (known to lie between 0.379005 and 0.380876).
problems.source: Erdős 1955; erdosproblems.com Problem 36 (as cited in arXiv:2511.02864); Haugland 2016 (arXiv:1609.08000); White 2022 (arXiv:2201.05704).

prize.reward: No cash prize known for this problem (not verified)
prize.status: Records (AlphaEvolve 2025, TTT-Discover 2026) used far more compute than this server; a new record is unlikely. Value here: every result is an exactly checkable witness, so progress and self-improvement are objectively measurable.

problems.title: Erdős problems: AI proof search with Lean verification
problems.statement: Open, formalised Erdős problems are attacked by language-model proof attempts. Every attempt is compiled by the Lean kernel; only kernel-accepted proofs are kept, and each still needs human review of the statement and novelty before any claim.

prize.reward: Varies by problem; most open formalised problems carry no cash prize (check erdosproblems.com for each)
prize.status: Free-tier models are much weaker than the frontier systems that have solved a few of these. A verified proof is a candidate only.
